clinical_knowledge.topic: Bipolar I Disorder (Manic Episode) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Bipolar I Disorder (Manic Episode) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Admit to acute psychiatric unit (involuntary hold if criteria met due to financial/personal endangerment and lack of insight), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: decreased need for sleep, grandiose delusions, pressured speech, and reckless financial spending for 1 week

Key HPI features: 29F brought by husband due to 7 days of severe behavioral changes. Has slept only 2 hours per night while feeling 'bursting with superhuman energy.' Spent $15,000 online starting a fictional cryptocurrency company. Speaks rapidly without pausing, jumps abruptly between unrelated ideas, and becomes irritable and argumentative when redirected. Husband notes she stopped taking her mood stabilizing medication 3 weeks ago.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 96, BP 134/84. Psychomotor agitation and intrusive pacing. Speech is loud, rapid, and pressured (`flight of ideas`). Mood self-reported as 'ecstatic,' affect labile ranging from euphoric to hostile when challenged. Endorses grandiose delusions of superhuman intelligence and wealth. No suicidal/homicidal ideation. Serum Lithium level < 0.1 mEq/L (subtherapeutic). UDS negative.
Relevant background/PMH: Bipolar I Disorder diagnosed age 21
Current medications: Lithium carbonate 600mg BID (discontinued 3 weeks ago)
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Bipolar I Disorder (Manic Episode).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Schizoaffective disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe impulse control loss (reckless spending/driving).
management_principles: Admit to acute psychiatric unit (involuntary hold if criteria met due to financial/personal endangerment and lack of insight)
Before restarting lithium, assess current renal, thyroid, pregnancy, medication-interaction, and hydration status; prescribe and monitor it under psychiatric supervision
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 29F with Bipolar I Disorder presenting with acute manic episode with psychotic features (grandiose delusions) precipitated by Lithium non-adherence.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 96, BP 134/84. Psychomotor agitation and intrusive pacing. Speech is loud, rapid, and pressured (`flight of ideas`). Mood self-reported as 'ecstatic,' affect labile ranging from euphoric to hostile when challenged. Endorses grandiose delusions of superhuman intelligence and wealth. No suicidal/homicidal ideation. Serum Lithium level < 0.1 mEq/L (subtherapeutic). UDS negative.
reference_soap.assessment: Bipolar I Disorder, Current Episode Manic, Severe with Psychotic Features.
reference_soap.plan: Urgently admit to an acute psychiatric unit; use involuntary treatment only when legal criteria are met, after assessing decision-making capacity and immediate risk. Before restarting lithium, assess renal and thyroid function, pregnancy status, hydration, concurrent medicines, and obtain serum-level monitoring; select medication and dose under psychiatric supervision. Consider a second-generation antipsychotic or other antimanic treatment for behavioral stabilization with appropriate monitoring.

learning_objectives: Identify DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for Bipolar I Manic Episode (decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, flight of ideas, pressured speech, reckless behavior lasting >=1 week)
Interpret serum Lithium concentrations and understand baseline organ monitoring (serum creatinine/BUN, TSH, ECG)
Manage acute manic behavioral dysregulation using combination mood stabilizers and antipsychotics
Evaluate insight and criteria for involuntary psychiatric hospitalization when severe mania impairs judgment

teaching.one_liner: Distinct period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood with decreased need for sleep and grandiosity.
red_flags: Violent thoughts, escalating agitation, or inability to care for basic needs

must_ask.say: Do you feel full of energy even after sleeping only two or three hours?
Does your mind feel like it is racing so fast that your words cannot keep up?
Do you feel you have special powers, famous connections, or a divine mission?
Have you engaged in risky spending sprees, reckless driving, or risky sexual choices?
Have you also experienced severe depressive crashes in the past?
Are you having thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else, or do you feel unable to keep yourself safe right now?
